narr: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
ev: Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sheets Gulch.
Runoff from a heavy rain event over the Coal Hollow Fire Burn Scar flowed over railroad tracks and onto the south shoulder of U.S. Highway 6.
Heavy rain over the Ether Hollow Fire Burn Scar produced a debris flow that moved across Quiet Meadows Lane on the outskirt of Mapleton.
Zion National Park officials reported flash flooding in both the main canyon and in tributaries feeding the canyon from the east.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sulphur Creek, with water running 6-12 inches high. Also flash flooding occurred in the Fremont River and Grand Wash.
Urban flash flooding was reported in Cedar City. A video received via social media showing water flowing down streets near the Ashdown Subdivision.
Flash flooding occurred in a tributary of Shoal Creek. An abandoned pickup truck was observed submerged in the water.
A Capitol Reef National Park official shared a video of flash flooding in Sulphur Creek.
Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported flash flooding along the Escalante River and Calf Creek.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise of 397 CFS, or about 1.5 feet.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a 3 foot rise, with peak flows of 1800 CFS.
Flash flooding washed out the main access road to Old Irontown from State Route 56. Emergency managers stated the road was closed until repaired.
Water and debris flowed across State Route 21.

Beaver County dispatch and emergency management personnel reported street flooding in Milford with water 3 feet deep. In addition, debris from flooding was reported on State Route 21 near Milford. The Milford automated weather station recorded 1.10 inches of rain in one hour.
A weather spotter reported water running down streets in Tropic.
